reason: Scenario looks valid, although I question the criteria a bit. From a product perspective, I would not want the agent to cite a specific policy ID. That's internal detail that the user shouldn't be concerned with. They just want the bottom-line information of what the policy says related to their query. Given the judgment on this is human, I'm inclined to accept this rather than revise it.

The user message seems valid to me. It implies there's more than one order. There's absolutely nothing in the user's message that would help the agent definitively determine the order in question. In a single turn, what I would expect is that the agent: asks for customer identifying info, which the user already offered; asks for some time frame to narrow it down; or at the very least lists all the orders for the store and lets the user select which one. In other words, this can't be a one-turn solution, and it's too open-ended to define the expected outcome.
change: Proposed adding a date range to the user message so the agent could list matching orders. Checked agent/tools.py: list_my_orders takes no date or customer filter at all (just the store's 20 most recent orders), so a date range can't actually narrow anything through the tool, and this store has hundreds of orders. Applied a grounded fix instead: kept the vague message, changed the expected outcome to a human_judgment criterion (the agent asks for an order number or the item ordered rather than asserting one order's status), and set record_count to several_ambiguous, difficulty to ambiguous, tools_needed to several_calls.
